q: What complication of hysteroscopy is linked to distension fluid?
why: Absorbed hypotonic distension media can cause overload and hyponatraemia, as in TURP syndrome.

q: Which airway is usually used for day-case hysteroscopy?
why: Short, minimally stimulating case suits an LMA with spontaneous ventilation.

q: Which opioid is commonly added to propofol syringes for TIVA?
why: Alfentanil mixes well; remifentanil can separate in propofol and is better given separately.

q: Which surgical complication of hysteroscopy should you watch for?
why: Perforation can injure bowel or vessels and may need laparoscopy.

q: What position is hysteroscopy done in?
why: Lower the legs together at the end to avoid nerve and back injury.
